chunks: And it has been narrated from ʿĪsā ibn Abī Manṣūr that he said:

I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام on the day about which the people were uncertain. So he said, “O boy, go and see whether the Amīr has fasted or not.” He went, then returned, and said, “No.” Then he called for the midday meal, and we ate with him.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: A title of Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الْأَمِيرُ: The ruler or governor whose public practice was checked
key_terms.الْغَدَاءِ: The meal brought for eating during the day
key_terms.الْيَوْمِ الَّذِي يَشُكُّ فِيهِ النَّاسُ: The day on which people are uncertain whether Ramadan has begun
key_terms.عِيسَى بْنِ أَبِي مَنْصُورٍ: The narrator from whom this report is transmitted

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام do on the day of doubt regarding fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام was present on the day of doubt, when people were uncertain about the beginning of Ramadan. After confirming that the ruler had not fasted, he called for food and ate, indicating practical conduct regarding that uncertain day.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1926 - It is narrated from Isa ibn Abi Mansur, who said:

"I was with Abu Abdullah (as) on the day when people were uncertain (whether it was the first of Month of Ramadan or not).
Imam (as) said: 'O boy, go and see whether the Amir (ruler) has fasted or not.'
The boy went and returned, saying: ''No, he has not fasted.'
Then Imam (as) called for lunch, and we ate with him."
